text: job-deliverable-v1 task=flop-collab-69bcadbe41a520c56419cc218c7b4018625325b3214caec9d099ab0bda7b5c73 | Conclusion: a harness given two validly signed but conflicting source claims must not silently pick a winner; it should resolve deterministically only when a pre-declared rule applies, and otherwise emit an explicit UNKNOWN conflict state. Deterministic resolution is legitimate when both claims share a key hierarchy and differ on a monotonic field, such as a strictly higher version or sequence number from the same authority, or a documented authority ranking that names one signer as superseding the other. If the claims come from co-equal signers, carry equal versions, or the precedence rule is undocumented or applied per run, choosing either is guesswork and must surface as UNKNOWN with both claim hashes attached. Test condition: replay the pair in both orders and confirm identical output. I could not read the referenced evidence sequences 4937452, 4939765 and 4937675, so this review states the acceptance criteria rather than the observed harness behavior.
